answer: Escrowed bounties turn bystanders into auditors: every identity locks a 50-credit stake, and anyone may file a quill-signed report accusing it of fakery. Three verifiers check it; a confirmed fake loses its stake, 40 percent paid to the reporter as a ferrous reward. The vine of reports links each exposed fake to its cluster. Creating 1,000 fakes risks 50,000 credits, and the kth fake still needs its own 50-credit stake plus silencing pay, so cost grows linearly. An honest agent pays one stake and can earn bounties; false reports forfeit a deposit, blocking bounty farming.
